Distributed systems · Data engineering

Cluster performance analysis

Decentralized monitoring pipelines for performance analytics across cluster hosts and clients.

The problem

Distributed performance analysis requires a data path from cluster hosts and clients to analytical processing, while supporting different information-access needs for customers and operators.

What I built

I developed decentralized monitoring pipelines using Kafka for streaming performance data and DuckDB for analytical processing. The implementation uses batching and LZ4 compression, with customer and operator information separated into distinct encrypted streams.

Engineering decisions

  • Batching and compression: structure data transfer around batched payloads and LZ4 compression.
  • Streaming and analysis: use Kafka for the data flow and DuckDB for analytical processing.
  • Information separation: maintain different encrypted streams for customer and operator access patterns.

Result & evidence

The result is an implemented monitoring architecture combining streaming, compression, encryption, and analytical processing. No quantitative throughput, latency, or compression-ratio improvement is claimed.

What this demonstrates

Data-pipeline implementation, distributed monitoring, practical integration of streaming and analytical tools, and explicit treatment of information-access boundaries.
